source.title: How Do Linear Probes Emerge? A Circuit-Tracing Framework with Concept-Targeted Attribution
source.authors: V. Palit; Florent Draye; Terry Jingchen Zhang; B. Schölkopf; Zhi-Jing Jin

page_placements.theme: Functional and graph-level descriptions beyond atom identity

record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse-feature attribution to LLMs and reports results about whether CLT features and their circuits account for probe-readable concepts. It does not reproduce the original toy-network method.
record.gate_note: The study measures CLT-based sparse-feature circuits and their effects on probe scores, graph consistency, and probe predictability. It does not test toy-model superposition, capacity competition, neuron polysemanticity, or whether features overlap as nearly orthogonal directions. Probe accuracies and feature statistics used to select layers or features are not separately recorded unless they are part of a reported analysis.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained Cross-Layer Transcoders as a tool to build probe-targeted attribution graphs. It reports its own method's results: probe/logit circuit dissociation, graph structure predicting probe accuracy, and feature recurrence across prompts and layers. It never tests whether features are superposed, whether the dictionary recovers the model's features (no reconstruction, sparsity or completeness measures), or whether dictionary features are canonical across dictionaries. No row measures what any of V1–V6 names.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that concept encoding and generation recruit causally separable circuits in both models. Probe-targeted graphs vary across prompts but converge on a shared feature core, and their structure predicts probe accuracy. They flag CLT quality (conflated, omitted or polysemantic features) and binary feature presence as limits.
record.recipe_differences: Uses linear-probe-targeted attribution graphs and Cross-Layer Transcoders in LLMs, rather than toy networks trained and analyzed for superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by concept, model, and layer. Truthfulness is less cleanly dissociated; Llama-3.2-1B has weak Sentiment and Truthfulness probe trajectories and weaker within-concept structural predictability than Gemma-2-2B.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating probe-exclusive attribution nodes lowers the probe score with 0% token flips in most concept/model pairs. Ablating logit-exclusive nodes flips tokens in 92–100% of cases with ∆S≈0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept-representation and token-generation circuits in LLMs are causally separable.

fits_no_version.finding: Binary presence of CLT features predicts probe margins well for Toxicity (ρ up to 0.86) but poorly for Sentiment (R2 0.08 at L21) and Reasoning (peak R2 0.14).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear-probe concept directions are explained by a small set of sparse dictionary features.

fits_no_version.finding: Top predictive features recur 6–21× above random across prompts, and graph overlap across adjacent layers reaches about 0.9.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept attribution graphs share a stable feature core across prompts and layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Graph-structural features predict probe validation accuracy (Gemma ρ 0.91; Llama raw ρ 0.81, within-concept ρ 0.34).

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Only two model sizes/families are tested. Causal ablations use 50 prompts per concept. The authors state that CLTs can conflate, omit, or represent features polysemantically, and that feature-presence analysis omits activation magnitude; the study does not establish feature completeness or canonicality.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or overlap geometry.
No capacity or polysemanticity analysis of neurons.
No analysis of the origins of polysemantic neurons.
Uses CLT features as given; does not measure feature spread across neurons or the dictionary's recovery of sparse features.
No comparison across dictionaries, sizes or seeds; no completeness measure. The authors note the CLT may conflate or omit features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T3/tests classification and its V4/V5 labels are rejected. CLT features are a tool here, and the measured constructs are probe/logit circuit dissociation and graph consistency, not superposition or dictionary-feature canonicality. The near-orthogonal probe directions (max |cos| 0.069) come after Gram-Schmidt on probe directions and are not evidence on V1. R29 and R35 duplicate one result.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, feature sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular overlap geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemantic neurons or allocates dedicated dimensions to important features.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
The study uses CLT features rather than SAE features, and does not measure feature spread across neurons or establish that superposition explains the features.
The study measures recurrence and graph stability, but does not establish that dictionary features are complete or canonical units of the model.
Whether the represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional subspaces.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Predicted probe score margins from binary presence of top-100 activation-ranked CLT features using Ridge regression.
rows.measure: Spearman correlation between predicted and actual probe score margins
rows.value: ρ above 0.66 at every layer; peak 0.86 at L10
rows.note: The paper says the signal is largely explained by a small set of early-layer lexical features.
rows.check: Predicts probe margin from binary presence of the top-100 CLT features. This is about probe readout, not whether the model holds sparse superposed features.

rows.note: The authors report that individual feature presence does not recover polarity reliably.

source_check.correct: Table 5 states the de-meaned layer baseline: ρ = +0.587; R2 = +0.240. GB: ρ = +0.925; R2 = +0.850. Table 6 separately reports observed de-meaned ρ = +0.908, CI [+0.817, +0.962], p < 0.005.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Measured consecutive-layer Jaccard overlap between CTA graphs for a representative prompt per concept.
rows.measure: Consecutive-layer graph-feature Jaccard J(L, L − 1)
rows.value: J stabilizes at approximately 0.9 between layers 8–12 and remains there through final layers
rows.note: The paper describes rapid early feature turnover followed by stabilization; the figure shows representative prompts.
rows.check: Jaccard overlap of attribution graphs across adjacent layers for one representative prompt. This is circuit stability, not stability or canonicality of dictionary features across dictionaries (V5).

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Measured how often top predictive features recur in CTA graphs across prompts.

conditions.value: 100 prompts at belief and highest-accuracy layers

rows.measure: Presence-rate enrichment of top predictive features over random features
rows.baseline: Expected presence rate of a random feature
rows.value: Top predictive features appear 6–21 times more often than a random feature
rows.note: The authors report a shared feature core alongside prompt-level divergence at the graph periphery; this supports recurrence but does not establish canonical or complete units.
rows.check: Cross-prompt recurrence of top predictive features within one CLT. It does not bear on whether SAE features are complete or canonical units. Duplicate of R29.

relation.reason: Sparse feature decomposition supplies the method's units; dictionary completeness, canonicality, capacity pressure and superposition geometry are not evaluated.

tranche.reason: Uses CLT features for concept-targeted attribution and reports circuit dissociation and predictor performance; it does not directly test a superposition claim version.

source_check.notes: These rows measure the study's predictor performance, so cannot_determine with no version links is appropriate. Tables 5–6 and 8–9 report differing observed correlations; preserve their separate provenance.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.2-1B; CTA feature ablations and feature-level analyses
reader_labels.reason: Ablating probe-specific sparse nodes changes internal probe scores while generally preserving generated tokens, and recurrent CLT features predict probe margins; see R1, R4, R7, R13, R16, R19, R25, R29.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Truthfulness ablations and feature-level prediction; especially Llama-3.2-1B Truthfulness at L1
reader_labels.reason: Truthfulness shows weaker or shared circuit effects, Llama’s L1 truthfulness probe-exclusive ablation has near-zero effect, and some feature-level predictors are weak; see R10, R12, R22, R24, R27, R28, R33.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Measured cross-layer stability and top-feature recurrence in Gemma-2-2B
reader_labels.reason: CTA graph overlap stabilizes at approximately 0.9 in later layers, and top predictive features recur much more often than random features; see R34 and R35.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across prompts and concepts in Gemma-2-2B
reader_labels.reason: The reported consistency is a shared feature core, not uniform canonical circuits: graphs diverge at the periphery, enrichment varies by concept, and the paper notes CLT conflation, omissions, and polysemantic features; see R29 and R35.
